purpose: Flavoxate helps relieve uncomfortable symptoms related to bladder and urinary tract problems, such as painful urination, frequent urges to go, and bladder spasms. It is used to treat symptoms caused by urinary tract infections, bladder inflammation, or other urinary conditions. It does not treat the infection itself, just the discomfort.
how_it_works: Your bladder is a muscle, and sometimes it can squeeze too hard or at the wrong times, causing pain and urgency. Flavoxate works by relaxing the muscles of your bladder so it does not contract as forcefully or as often. This helps reduce that sudden urge to urinate, cramping, and burning sensations.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, dizziness, headache, drowsiness, and an upset stomach are the most common side effects. Some people may also notice a fast heartbeat or constipation. These effects are usually mild.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have a blockage in your stomach, intestines, or urinary tract, or if you have glaucoma. It can cause blurred vision and dizziness, so be careful driving or operating machinery. Tell your doctor if you have any eye problems, fever, or if your symptoms do not improve. Older adults should use this medication with caution as side effects may be more noticeable.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg to 200 mg taken three to four times a day by mouth. Your doctor will tell you the exact dose that is right for you. Try to take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day, and always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions.
